items.title: Unify the two blank-value predicates (lib/answered.js isBlank vs model/engine/is-blank-value.js)
items.detail: Two blank checks with different semantics judge the two sides of the same boundary: lib/answered.js isBlank trims strings and recurses composites to any depth; model/obligations/is-blank-value.js isBlankValue does not trim and checks one composite level. ' ' (whitespace) and a nested all-empty composite are blank to one and content to the other — exactly the divergence class the is-blank-value extraction existed to kill. From scratch: one predicate. The model import boundary permits lib/ -> model/ (obligation-purity restricts only model's own imports), so lib/answered.js can derive isAnswered from isBlankValue. DECISION NEEDED: which semantics win (trim or not; deep or one-level) — the choice is user-visible at the margins (a whitespace-only text answer; a cleared nested composite). RECOMMENDATION: single definition in model/obligations/is-blank-value.js extended to trim + full depth (the stricter union, matching user intuition of 'blank'), lib/answered.js re-exports; verify against the status/purge test suites for edge flips.

items.title: Dual-key bug: bridge/status.js domain lookup by name against a UUID-keyed registry always misses — and the miss is load-bearing
items.detail: Found while producing the p-101 decision doc. bridge/status.js:155 calls domain.get(name) against the UUID-keyed domain registry (model/domain/index.js:106), so the lookup ALWAYS misses and statusOf's partial-address handling silently falls back to isBlankValue. The miss is currently load-bearing: the domain's required sub-fields do not match the stored top-level address shape, so 'fixing' the lookup naively would change address status behaviour. Needs a ruling on intended semantics (should partial-address status use domain.isComplete — and if so the domain shape needs aligning first — or is the isBlankValue fallback the intended behaviour, in which case the dead lookup should be deleted)? Interacts with p-101 (key shape) and p-106 (blank semantics: domain.isComplete trims, isBlankValue does not).
items.evidence: bridge/status.js:156 (was :155); model/domain/index.js:106,54-64; bridge/collection-complete.js:47-53 (correct sibling path); decision-docs/p-101-answers-shape.md (surprise finding 1)
items.decision: RE-CHECKED by orchestrator 2026-07-24 after p-101/p-106 landed: NOT fixed by option-e. bridge/status.js:156 still does domain.get(name) where name is an obligation NAME (toStructural sets .id=obligation.name at status.js:91), while domain is keyed by obligation.id (UUID) — so the lookup always misses and top-level addresses fall through to !isBlankValue. Effect: a partially-filled address (one non-blank field) shows its task row as FULFILLED and CYA does not prompt 'complete the address', contradicting model/domain/index.js:7-11. bridge/collection-complete.js:48 already does domain.get(obligationId) with the real UUID (proves the stored address shape matches ADDRESS_REQUIRED_SUB_FIELDS), so this is a one-line divergence. RULED by Sam 2026-07-24: FIX + add test — align status.js's domain lookup to the obligation id (mirror collection-complete.js), restoring partial-address -> In-progress, and add the missing partial top-level-address status regression test (no such fixture exists today). | RE-OPENED by orchestrator 2026-07-24: the 'safe one-liner' premise was WRONG. Building it surfaced that model/domain/index.js's isComplete is STALE — it validates a FLAT address shape (name/addressLine1/town/postcode/country/telephone/email at top level) that no longer matches the real stored shape. Addresses bind as scalars (features/addresses/evaluation.js), so state.fulfilments[consignor.id] is the raw stored value = nested { name, address: { addressLine1, townOrCity, county, postcode, country, telephoneNumber, emailAddress } } from create-address.controller.js:114-123 (and loose { addressLine1, addressLine2, addressLine3, country } from party-picker/MDM fixtures like happy-path.json:40-48). isComplete checks value.addressLine1 / value.town (undefined on the nested shape) so EVERY complete real address would evaluate INCOMPLETE -> row stuck in-progress -> journey never ready -> cannot submit. The one-line fix (domain.get(obligationFor(name)?.id)) makes the lookup HIT and thereby breaks real addresses; Codex's attempt masked this by replacing happy-path.json's real addresses with flat-keyed fixtures (unit suite green on fiction; real journey + E2E would fail). ALSO ESTABLISHED: create-address re-renders 400 without committing when any required field is missing (controller.js:134-139) and party-picker addresses are complete-by-source, so a PARTIAL top-level address is effectively unreachable in the real journey — the domain's partial-address gate is redundant in practice and !isBlankValue (non-empty) is an accurate 'fulfilled' proxy. Codex attempt stashed in worktree (git stash: 'p-115 codex attempt'), worktree reverted clean. NEEDS a fresh ruling — the real choice is (A) realign the domain isComplete to the real nested address shape + fix the lookup (and decide which sub-fields = complete across create-address vs MDM entry paths — a further Sam/Paul shape question), or (B) delete the stale domain isComplete apparatus and ratify !isBlankValue (deletes merge residue; gating is redundant given per-page validation). Orchestrator now leans (B). | RULED by Sam 2026-07-24: OPTION B — delete the address isComplete gate; addresses use !isBlankValue like every other obligation (isComplete was address-only special-casing). FURTHER FINDINGS behind the ruling: every address is stored NESTED { name, address: {...} } (party addresses via create-address.controller.js / party-picker; permanentAddress per-unit via animal-identification.controller.js:483-493) while the domain's required lists are FLAT — so the gate is stale everywhere. status.js's lookup was NAME-keyed (always missed -> !isBlankValue), but collection-complete.js:48 looks up by the real UUID so its gate is LIVE for permanentAddress (within: unitRecord) and currently marks even a FILLED permanentAddress incomplete — a latent inconsistency vs status.js (which treats it complete). B unifies both consumers on !isBlankValue, deleting the disagreement. BUILD SCOPE: delete model/domain/index.js + index.test.js; drop the domain import + address branch in bridge/status.js (isValueFulfilled -> !isBlankValue) and bridge/collection-complete.js (isFulfilled -> !isBlankValue); drop domain from obligation-purity.js assertNoDisplayKeys (guard KEPT, only its domain arg goes) + fix obligation-purity.test.js:32 fixture; remove the real-domain assertions in model/no-display-keys.test.js (keep the synthetic negative test) and delete the 'domain carries address entries' describe in model/obligations/coverage.test.js; update the domain/isComplete address-completeness passages in docs (obligation-model.md, validation.md, architecture.md, add-a-field.md, testing.md, limits.md, decisions.md, README.md). Behaviour: status.js unchanged; collection-complete addresses flip incomplete->complete-when-filled (aligns to status.js). Verify unit + FULL E2E incl. a Cat/permanent-address journey. | BUILT + TESTED + LANDED 2026-07-24 (commit 3471b14 on spike/EUDPA-288-model-retrofit, ff-pushed + pulled into Sam's checkout). Deleted model/domain/ (index.js + index.test.js); rewired bridge/status.js + bridge/collection-complete.js to !isBlankValue; dropped the domain arg from the KEPT obligation-purity display-key guard (model/no-display-keys.js) + repointed obligation-purity.test.js's intra-model import fixture; removed the domain describe in model/obligations/coverage.test.js + the real-domain assertions in model/no-display-keys.test.js (negative control preserved, re-anchored on a synthetic nested obligation); collection-complete.test.js address fixture corrected to the REAL nested shape (multi-unit still [true,true], now pinning the intended behaviour honestly — no masking); refreshed 10 docs. items.title: Multi-tab session interference: the active journey id is a single yar value, not carried in the URL
items.detail: Raised by Sam + Paul Hodgson (chat 2026-07-24): with yar/Redis session storage keyed by the session-id cookie, a user with the journey open in multiple tabs (different notifications) gets last-write-wins interference between tabs. ROOT CAUSE (traced): the notification/journey RECORDS are backend-backed keyed by journeyId (fine), and FLOW_ONLY_ANSWERS is ALREADY sub-keyed by journeyId (services/persistence/session/real.js:56-68, { [journeyId]: values }) — so Paul's suggested sub-key structure is already applied there. The remaining defect is that ACTIVE_JOURNEY (and OPENING_RUN) are SINGLE session-global values (real.js:3,5,26-31,48-53) and the current journey is resolved from ACTIVE_JOURNEY, NOT from the URL (engine/journey.js:64-70 currentJourney -> session.activeJourneyId). So tab B selecting notification Y overwrites ACTIVE_JOURNEY, and tab A's next request loads Y — that single wrong journeyId then also poisons the correctly-sub-keyed flow-only reads. FIX DIRECTION: carry the notification/journey id in the URL (path segment) per tab so each tab is self-identifying, retire the single ACTIVE_JOURNEY pointer (and OPENING_RUN handling), leaving the already-per-journey session sub-keying to work correctly per tab. Interlocks with auth/per-user scoping (p-012/p-025) and the URL/routing structure. Sam: 'matters for both tickets (obligations frontend and document upload)' — the document-upload flow (ownsUpload / upload page state) is session-backed and would corrupt across tabs the same way. ROUTING: architectural — a first-class Lane E promotion-plan input (URL structure + session model + auth), not a quick prototype patch. Lane E to size and sequence it.
